messages:
anya: Quick intake — bringing up atlas-7b-instruct-2026 for production evaluation. primary ask: prioritize a compact quantization path that preserves instruction-following quality for chat workloads. thinking: gguf packed + selective fp8 on attention, fallback int8-static for CPU targets. any blockers?
liam: +1. do we have the fine-tune/export artifacts? need the pytorch state_dict and tokenizer config.
devon: I grabbed the export from training: s3://redwood-models/atlas/7b/v2026/export.tar.gz. includes model.safetensors, vocab.json, config.json.
sophia: fyi, we should also run the standard regression promptset (redwood/regressions/chat-instruct) before and after each quant run. threshold: <=1.5% ROUGE-L relative drop and <2% hallucination rate.
anya: thanks. plan proposal: 1) gguf quantize default (8-bit per-tensor) -> eval suite 2) int8-static calibration with 1k calibration steps (representative prompts) -> eval 3) hybrid fp8 attention + gguf weight pack -> eval 4) cost/latency bench on dedicated and hosted. prioritize (1,3,2) unless calibration failure.
liam: why (1,3,2) ordering?
anya: gguf is fastest to iterate (no custom kernel), gives big size wins. hybrid fp8 promising for latency on GPU; int8-static calibration takes ops to get right — lower priority unless gguf/hybrid regression unacceptable.
devon: quick sanity check — running a tiny gguf conversion to estimate size. command I ran: ```python -m rw_quant.pack_model --in model.safetensors --out atlas-7b.gguf --dtype 8bit``` output: "atlas-7b.gguf: 3.6G (was 13.2G)"
sophia: nice. can you run redwood-eval on a subset? something like: ```redwood-eval --model atlas-7b.gguf --prompts redwood/regressions/chat-instruct/1000.jsonl --metrics rouge-l,accuracy,healthiness --out gguf-1000.json```
devon: just did a 100-sample run, quick numbers: gguf vs fp16 baseline -> ROUGE-L -0.9%, instr-follow acc -0.6pp, latency per-token +6% (higher single-token cost but batching improves).
anya: that looks promising. any hallucination flags?
devon: hallucination heuristic (url-check + factuality model) flagged 2/100 for gguf, baseline had 1/100. within threshold per sophia.
liam: on hybrid fp8: do we have kernels ready on our runtime? eng-runtime had an fp8 branch last quarter. I can prod eng-runtime to get a canary image for benching.
anya: please do. also need a short checklist for onboarding so we can move this model to dedicated rollout if it passes. my checklist draft: - artifacts present (safetensors, tokenizer) - baseline eval (fp16) completed - gguf conversion + eval - hybrid fp8 run (GPU) + eval - int8-static calibration (if needed) - latency & cost benchmarks across configs - canary rollout config (1% traffic) - monitoring hooks (token-level cost, hallucination alerts) - rollback policy defined
sophia: add: export model card with explicit quant notes and expected repro script. and add eval seed/commit id for reproducibility.
devon: I hit a small issue: gguf conversion reorders keys, our tokenizer loader needs "model_prefix" fix. patch diff: ```+ tokenizer.load_pretrained(prefix='atlas-7b')``` — want to push PR to devex before big test?
liam: go ahead, small PR ok. put integration test in CI that loads gguf and runs a smoke generation.
anya: timeline: aiming to finish gguf + quick eval by EOD tomorrow, hybrid fp8 by Friday, int8 cal next week if needed. anyone object?
sophia: sounds good. I'll prepare the regression list and gating criteria doc and drop link here once ready.
devon: kicked off a 1k prompt gguf eval in the background, will post results when done. eval-bot: redwood-eval job 82347 started (model=atlas-7b.gguf, sample_count=1000)
liam: once the 1k run lands, can someone run batchbench across 256-token and 1024-token scenarios on both dedicated and hosted? I want tail latency percentiles (p50,p95,p99) and cost per 1M tokens.
anya: noted. whoever runs batchbench, please include KV cache memory use and peak GPU mem. also capture sequence-length distribution we used.
sophia: uploaded the gating doc draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/onboarding/atlas-7b-2026-quant-gate (will update after more results) :memo:
devon: 1k gguf eval finished: summary -> ROUGE-L -1.0%, instr-acc -0.8pp, hallucination 1.9%, avg latency/token 0.94x baseline (batched 16), size 3.6G. attaching raw: s3://ci-artifacts/82347/gguf-1000.json
liam: looks within gating. next: run hybrid fp8 canary on GPU canary image. pinging @eng-runtime for image.
anya: thanks all. I'll create the onboarding ticket with the checklist and link results once we have hybrid numbers. :rocket:
